title: DelegationEnvelope v1
description: A narrow, scoped, single-use proof that one component (issuer) may ask a specific other component/boundary (audience) to act on behalf of a specific actor, for exactly one ExecutionRequest. Does NOT implement cryptographic signing itself (Section 7) -- auth_assertion_ref points to wherever that proof actually lives; this schema only defines the shape and the validation rules around it (expiry, audience matching, single-use nonce, single-request binding).

issuer.description: The component asserting this delegation, e.g. IVE. Actor-shaped (not a bare string) so the issuer's own identity requires a resolvable auth_ref -- fixed after Codex adversarial review (Finding F-02) found that a bare issuer string let any caller simply declare itself e.g. 'aef_policy_engine' with no binding to anything a future AEF could independently resolve, a textbook confused-deputy setup. type='user' is never valid for an issuer (enforced in validators.ts, not expressible in this $ref alone) -- only a service or system component may issue a delegation.

subject.description: Whose intent this delegation represents -- same Actor shape as ExecutionRequest, same rule: id alone proves nothing without auth_ref.

audience.description: The SPECIFIC execution boundary this delegation authorizes reaching, e.g. 'aef.core.action_engine', 'aef.quant.controlled_live', 'aef.stripe.billing'. A delegation for one audience must never be accepted for another -- an IVE->AEF delegation for 'aef.core' does not, and structurally cannot per validators.ts, satisfy a request whose domain/action maps to 'aef.quant.controlled_live' or 'aef.stripe.billing'. Each hop in a future chain (IVE->AEF, AEF->Stripe, AEF->Supabase Admin, AEF->Broker) needs its OWN delegation with that hop's own audience (Section 8). Matching against a request's domain is boundary-aware, not a plain prefix check: 'aef.core' matches domain=core, as does any '.'-delimited subcomponent like 'aef.core.action_engine' -- but 'aef.coreextra' does NOT match domain=core, even though it shares the same leading characters (Codex adversarial review, Finding F-03, fixed in validators.ts's validateRequestAgainstDelegation).

expires_at.description: Independent expiry from the ExecutionRequest's own expires_at -- both are checked, whichever is stricter governs.

nonce.description: Single-use value. A future AEF must reject any delegation whose nonce has been seen before (authentication-replay defense) -- see validators.ts's NonceStore interface, which this contract mission implements only as an in-memory reference for tests, explicitly NOT for production use.

purpose.description: Human/machine-readable statement of what this delegation is for. Descriptive, cross-checked against `scope`, never authoritative on its own.

scope.description: Explicit allow-list of action patterns this delegation covers, e.g. ['core.generate_strategy', 'core.knowledge_vault.*']. The ExecutionRequest's `action` must match at least one pattern here. Never a blanket '*' at the top level -- see validators.ts, which rejects a bare '*' scope entry outright.

request_binding.description: The exact request_id this delegation is bound to. v1 delegations are single-request only -- one delegation cannot satisfy two different ExecutionRequests, even within its own expiry window and scope. (A future v2 could consider multi-request delegations; deliberately not built here -- see README.)

auth_assertion_ref.description: Reference to wherever the actual cryptographic or session proof behind this delegation lives. This contract does not implement or validate the proof itself -- only requires its presence and that an independent component resolves it before trusting the rest of this envelope.
